clue.text: It keeps the house dry, it is often felt

definitions.text: It keeps the house dry, it is often felt

parts.words: It keeps the house dry, it is often felt
parts.note: a layer built into a wall near the ground to stop moisture rising, traditionally made of bituminous felt; 'felt' teases as the verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as the past tense of feel, as though damp is sensed; it is the roofing material such barriers were made from.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof layer near the base of a wall that blocks rising moisture is exactly what keeps a building dry.

clue.text: Double fare for the old bird?

indicators.note: double asks for the word for fare to be written twice in a row

parts.note: a do is a party or feast, food and drink laid on, so fare

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a double helping is the right meal for an aged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, an informal word for a party with food, said twice gives the extinct bird of Mauritius.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius is the classic example of a creature long gone.

clue.text: Stick to pig food

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep feeding swine their usual meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole or spar on a ship is a stick in one sense, and the nuts of beech and oak that pigs forage are the other.

clue.text: Smoker's down-and-out?

parts.note: the stub left of something smoked once it is finished, read as a tramp belonging to a smoker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-and-out' suggests a destitute person; here it is the burnt-down, thrown-out butt of a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt left when a smoke is finished is literally burnt down and thrown out.

clue.text: Employers' dishonest ruses

indicators.note: dishonest suggests the letters of ruses are crooked, bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Bosses are accused of underhand tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: People who employ something, putting it to use, are its consumers in the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Note lawful alternative for one who accosts people

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
licit means permitted by law
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A remark about the legal option for a person who stops strangers in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the old sense of the word: one who solicits, approaching people to ask for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who solicits approaches strangers with a request, the older meaning behind the lawyer's title.

clue.text: Business condition for capital cover

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A firm's terms for providing cover in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here is the head, from Latin caput, so a capital cover is a close-fitting cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cap worn on the head is a covering for the top of a person.

clue.text: District branch, not in Victoria, for example

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
Victoria is a major London railway station

explanation.surface: A regional office somewhere outside the Australian state of Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria suggests the Australian state; it is Victoria Station in London, so a station.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote post or office of an organisation, away from headquarters, is a branch in the provinces.

clue.text: Child may be transported by this Iolanthe sequence

definitions.text: Child may be transported by this

parts.note: Iolanthe is the fairy heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta
a cycle is a sequence of events or works, as in a song cycle

explanation.surface: A child might be enraptured by a run of Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests carried away with delight by the operetta; it means simply ridden on. A fairy cycle was a small child's bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bicycle made for young children was a way for a youngster to ride about.

clue.text: Deliberately sketched lady's extremities

parts.note: to design is to draw up plans, to sketch

indicators.note: extremities are the outermost parts, so the first and last letters of the word lady

explanation.surface: Someone sketched a woman's hands and feet on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after lady makes 'extremities' belong to her; the possessive adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by design means doing it intentionally, on purpose.

clue.text: The housewife's part in perpetuity

indicators.note: part in says the letters sit as a section within the word perpetuity

explanation.surface: A homemaker's role lasts forever.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'housewife' (pronounced hussif) is also a small sewing kit; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental case for needles and thread is what a sewing-kit hussif is.

clue.text: Yellow kind of solar gas that creeps low along the prairie

definitions.text: that creeps low along the prairie

parts.note: buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour

indicators.note: kind of suggests a variant form of solar gas, its letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: A yellowish sort of gas from the sun drifts low over the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges SOLARGAS into ALOGRASS after BUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing pasture plant of the North American plains spreads by runners along the ground.

clue.text: Not following the roads in Ireland?

explanation.surface: A question whether going off-road is the thing in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: IRE means anger, so Ire-land is punningly an angry nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling over open fields rather than along highways is one sense; an angry nation, punning on ire, is the other.

clue.text: Device sometimes used to make old books readable

definitions.text: Device sometimes used to make old books readable

parts.words: Device sometimes used to make old books readable
parts.note: older books were sold with folded pages uncut, so a blade was needed to slit them open before reading

explanation.walkthrough: Old volumes often came with uncut page edges; a blunt blade separated the leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt blade for slitting envelopes or uncut pages opened up books sold with their leaves still joined.

clue.text: Pinion and detain an old choker

parts.note: a pinion is a bird's wing
to collar someone is to seize and hold them

explanation.surface: Instructions to restrain and hold someone wearing old-fashioned neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choker' is old slang for a stiff high collar, not a strangler.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff upright neckband with turned-down points, worn with formal dress, squeezes the throat like a necklace that is tight.

clue.text: A substance intended, say, for feeding cattle for payment

parts.note: the gist is the substance or essence of something

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A substance meant as cattle feed is sold for a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you MEANT is only heard, spelt MENT here.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal term for taking in other people's livestock to graze on one's land for a fee.

clue.text: Old turn with cape has precision

parts.note: ex means former, old
an act or turn is a performance on stage
ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A veteran stage performer in a cape displays great accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' is a variety act on stage, not a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exactly right in every detail is accuracy, the quality of being precise.

clue.text: Unctuous, like Arbuckle

explanation.surface: Describing the silent film comedian as greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle was a silent-film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous means greasy or oily, and the silent comic Roscoe Arbuckle was famous under that nickname.

clue.text: Agree to alter the bore

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters of agree are changed in order

explanation.surface: Consenting to change the tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a dull person but a tidal wave surging up a river, as on the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge rushing up an estuary, such as the one on the Severn or Trent, is a bore.

clue.text: Sweet girl is first victim of the joker

parts.note: April is a girl's name
a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream

explanation.surface: A lovely girl is the first person a prankster fools.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of crushed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The person tricked on the first day of the fourth month is the joker's earliest dupe of the year.

clue.text: Won on knight's wrong move — what ignoramuses!

indicators.note: a wrong move on the chessboard, here shuffling the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: Someone won after a bad knight move in chess and scoffs at the dunces.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of knight's is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: People who know nothing are ignorant, and so are dunces; the term also named a US political party.

clue.text: Son lives with Susan

parts.note: lives here means exists, so is
Sue is short for Susan

explanation.surface: A boy lives with a woman called Susan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son' is the definition, not the abbreviation S: issue means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for offspring, a child of a parent.

clue.text: Objections raised to 3

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word for objections is written bottom to top

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Objections are brought up regarding something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 3 down: a butt left after smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: The short remnant of something smoked after use is a stub.

clue.text: Silver or gold, I'd say

parts.note: a freshwater fish found in silver and golden varieties, the latter popular in ornamental ponds

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a choice between metals; it is a fish found in silver and golden forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish related to the carp, the ide, is kept in golden and silver forms in ponds.

clue.text: Girl docked, returning to Capri

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the shortened name is read backwards
docked means cut short, like a tail, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Elsie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's ship docked on her way back to Capri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' drops the last E of ELSIE to give ELSI, and 'returning' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, a specific example of the category.

clue.text: He announces fresh information about the plant

parts.note: news is fresh information
c, for circa, means about
an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A man announces new facts concerning the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads the bulletins on radio or television is the person announcing the day's events.

clue.text: Goes astray and trespasses

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off course and intrudes on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trespasses' is meant in the biblical sense of sins.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off course is one sense, and to sin, as in the Lord's Prayer's trespasses, is the other.

clue.text: Professed to be one bit less troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of one bit less are stirred up

explanation.surface: Claimed to be a little less worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent or stated rather than real, as with a declared reason that may not be true.
